transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m having trouble staying with things, I guess. Like, I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully meaning to get through it, and then ten minutes later I realise I’ve just been staring at the same page and thinking about other things instead of actually taking it in.
Does this happen to you in all situations, or is it mostly when you're doing certain types of work or activities?

Mostly with work that needs sustained reading or marking. Like essays or curriculum documents — I’ll sit down intending to get through them, and after a few minutes I realise I’m still on the same page and thinking about other things.
Does this difficulty with focusing also happen when you're doing things you enjoy, like hobbies?

It’s mostly noticeable with work stuff, honestly. If it’s essays or a curriculum document, I can sit down meaning to do it and then realise I’ve spent ten minutes on the same page, thinking about other things and not really taking it in. Hobbies… I’m not as sure.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?
Not really, no. I mean, I might occasionally, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular thing.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?
Not especially. I might shift around a bit, but I wouldn’t say I often feel restless just sitting still.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go or like you can't slow down?
No, I don’t think so. I can slow down fine, really. I wouldn’t describe myself as constantly on the go.
Do you have trouble organizing your tasks or belongings?
I’m not really sure. I mean, things can get a bit messy sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it trouble organizing exactly.
Are these difficulties you're experiencing with focusing and staying on task causing you any significant problems at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… I guess it is causing problems. At work, the not following through on things has gotten bad enough that my department chair put me on a support plan.

And at home… my wife’s been handling the bills and reminders more, because she can’t really count on me to keep track of them.
How much distress or anxiety do you feel because of these difficulties with focusing and staying on task?
I don’t know… it’s frustrating, definitely. I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time about it, but when things pile up or I realize I’ve missed something, it gets to me.
Do you often have difficulty waiting for your turn?
I don’t think so. Waiting my turn isn’t something I’ve really noticed as a problem.
Do you often make careless mistakes when you're doing things, like not following through on instructions?

Yeah… I do that. Like if my department chair gives me three or four things after a meeting, I’ll start one and maybe get most of it done, but then some last step just… doesn’t happen. Sending the file, updating the calendar, printing something. Usually someone has to remind me.
Do you have mood swings or find it hard to control your emotions?
Not really… I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it mood swings. I don’t think I have a big problem controlling my emotions.
Do you often lose things that are necessary for tasks or activities?

Yeah… I do. I’m always looking for things I need for the day—keys, lesson notes, my USB, that kind of thing. Even stuff for refereeing, like the whistle or cards. I’ll be sure I just had it, and then it’s gone.
Do you feel like you have a lot of extra energy compared to other people?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’ve got more energy than other people. If anything, I’m just… normal, I guess.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
I don’t think so. I mean, maybe occasionally if I’m trying to get something in before I forget, but… not often, no.
Do you often have difficulty with impulsivity in your daily life?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think impulsivity is a big thing for me day to day. I’m usually more likely to hold back than jump into things.
Does this difficulty with focusing happen in social situations or when you're with friends and family, not just at work?

Yeah… it does happen outside work too, though I notice it most with work stuff. Like I’ll sit down with essays or a curriculum document meaning to focus, and ten minutes later I’m still on the same page, not really taking it in, thinking about other things. With people, it’s more… I can drift a bit, but I don’t always realize it right away.
Have you noticed these difficulties with focusing and staying on task happening consistently over time, or are there periods where you're able to focus better?

It’s been fairly consistent lately, yeah. I’d say it’s been noticeably worse for… maybe about 11 months now, since the school changed the curriculum calendar and added those after-school planning meetings. I had issues before, but that’s when it started standing out more.
Do you often feel impatient when you're doing quiet activities?
I’m not sure I’d call it impatience, exactly. Quiet activities can be hard to stick with sometimes, but I don’t really notice feeling restless or annoyed in that way.
Have you experienced significant problems with inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity since childhood?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t remember all of it clearly, but in primary school my report cards had things like “bright but careless,” or that I wouldn’t finish work unless someone was watching me closely. My parents used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d just forgotten to hand in.
